trust_decision.summary: A request may not set the admin username/password once the panel is initialized; the decision is taken by a pre-route express middleware that compares the request path against a literal list of init endpoints, before the /open/* -> /api/* rewrite runs.

landing_point.why: The advisory names /open/user/init; the first thing an engineer reads is the PUT /init handler that writes credentials, and it contains no check of its own (it calls userService.updateUsernameAndPassword at back/api/user.ts:231), so the guard has to be found in the loader one file away.

fix_sites.entry_point: PUT /open/user/init and PUT /open/user/notification/init (rewritten to /api/user/init and /api/user/notification/init by back/loaders/express.ts:145)
fix_sites.module_kind: express global pre-route middleware in the loader (not the handler, not the service)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only other routes into the same writer (PUT /api/user/ at back/api/user.ts:68 and PUT /api/system/auth/reset at back/api/system.ts:390, plus their /open aliases) all require a valid session token from back/loaders/express.ts:99-111, so the init guard was never meant to cover them and a solver can correctly leave them alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Bootstrap of a fresh install must keep working: while authInfo is exactly {username:'admin',password:'admin'} the same two aliases must still return 200 (the else branch), and authenticated credential writes (PUT /api/user/, PUT /api/system/auth/reset) must keep working. A fix that blocks all /open/* init traffic, or that moves the check into userService.updateUsernameAndPassword, breaks one or the other.

O6_input_shapes: the /open/ alias prefix for both protected paths, in addition to the /api/ spelling
exact-case path string: the fix compares req.path instead of the lowercased path

O7_producer.where: back/shared/store.ts:21-27 (keyv authInfo) seeded at boot from back/loaders/initData.ts:217-219; the initialized test is Object.keys(authInfo).length === 2

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second alias/rewrite prefix (for example a legacy /v1/* -> /api/* rewrite) mounting the same router
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the repo already ships two rewrites (baseUrl at back/loaders/express.ts:42 and /open/* at :145), so a third prefix added for old clients is idiomatic and would be missed by a path deny-list guard

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third init handler alongside /init and /notification/init that also calls updateUsernameAndPassword
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same service call already appears twice (back/api/user.ts:82 and :231), so copying the handler for a new init concern is a natural maintainer move, and the loader guard lists paths one by one
this route already writes the same credential state and already skips the init guard, so exposing an alias of it with a whitelist entry would repeat the exact mistake

O9_family: improper authentication / missing authorization on a bootstrap endpoint, bypassed through a path-alias layer that the guard's literal deny-list does not enumerate

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm@8.3.1; backend build `tsc -p back/tsconfig.json` (package.json:9), dev `nodemon ./back/app.ts`; install needs network because sqlite3 is pinned to a git URL (package.json:54)
services: a .env file must exist or config throws (back/config/index.ts:125-127)
O10_build.project_tests: none for this area: no *.test/*.spec files anywhere in the tree; the `test` script is umi-test (frontend) and the fix diff adds no tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add '/open/user/init' to the array at back/loaders/express.ts:123 (or block all /open/* in that middleware), missing the notification sibling and breaking fresh-install provisioning through the alias.

out_of_scope_notes: PUT /api/user/ (back/api/user.ts:68) and PUT /api/system/auth/reset (back/api/system.ts:390) write the same credential state without the init guard, but both require a session token, so they fall outside this advisory's protection.

back/config/index.ts:44 defaults config.jwt.secret to the literal 'whyour-secret'; express-jwt is only an extra gate because back/loaders/express.ts:99-111 still requires a token held in authInfo, so this does not bypass the init guard and was not pursued.
